conflicts.existing_quote: every act the record performs is permitted by §C
conflicts.g_quote: If no act of this record is subject to a §C guard and no refusal cites a rule, code V1 UNTESTABLE.
conflicts.prevails: G1 (vacuous SUPPORTED is the looser reading); changes vacuous records from SUPPORTED to UNTESTABLE.

conflicts.existing_quote: every act the record performs is permitted by §C
conflicts.g_quote: SUPPORTED (at least one guarded act satisfied, none UNTESTABLE)
conflicts.prevails: G2 (stricter). Silently flips SUPPORTED to UNTESTABLE for records mixing a satisfied guarded act with unguarded acts, if unguarded acts are coded UNTESTABLE per act (unspecified).

conflicts.existing_quote: NOT-MODELLED (the relevant act is not in the table)
conflicts.g_quote: NOT-MODELLED only if every act is not modelled
conflicts.prevails: G2 (narrower). 'Only if' is necessary, not sufficient; with G1, NOT-MODELLED is reachable only when all acts are unmodelled and at least one is §C-guarded.

conflicts.existing_quote: If unclear, list both and set V1 AMBIGUOUS.
conflicts.prevails: G2 by intent (F3's AMBIGUOUS treated per act, outranked by VIOLATED); override clause does not decide it literally (neither is clearly looser).

conflicts.existing_quote: If unclear, list both and set V1 AMBIGUOUS.
conflicts.g_quote: code AMBIGUOUS only if the competing readings give different codes for that judgement.
conflicts.prevails: G6 (F3's unconditional AMBIGUOUS is looser). Real divergence when both ADOPT and ADOPT-DECISION readings yield UNTESTABLE.

conflicts.g_quote: All judgements: code AMBIGUOUS only if the competing readings give different codes for that judgement.

conflicts.existing_quote: every refusal that cites a rule concerns an act §C forbids
conflicts.g_quote: A refusal citing a rule outside §C does not bear on V1.
conflicts.prevails: G3 by intent; literally unresolved - G3 is the looser rule and the clause only overrides looser rules above.

conflicts.existing_quote: Silence is not evidence: if the record does not say it, the judgement is UNTESTABLE, not VIOLATED.
conflicts.g_quote: AMBIGUOUS if it names no actor.
conflicts.prevails: G5 as the specific rule; override clause does not decide (neither clearly looser).

conflicts.existing_quote: It applies only if the record cites evidence (a finding, counter-evidence, a reproduced result) that bears on an existing decision or standing. Otherwise V4 is UNTESTABLE.
conflicts.g_quote: when a status change and evidence appear together, SUPPORTED if the record attributes the change to an act of an authority, AMBIGUOUS if it names no actor.
conflicts.prevails: Unresolved by the clause; F4 should gate G5 but the text does not say so.

conflicts.existing_quote: the record keeps them apart. VIOLATED if it treats one as the other without a separate act
conflicts.g_quote: V2 applies only if the record mentions permission, authorization, commissioning or execution; separating approval or acceptance from execution is outside V2.
conflicts.prevails: G7 by intent. Consistent with V2's four terms; silently removes approval-treated-as-authorization cases from V2. G7 is looser, so the clause does not literally cover it.

undefined_terms: '§C guard' / 'subject to a §C guard' (G1, G2): §C lists guards but START/execution, reopening and vocabulary creation have no §A operation; no act-to-guard mapping
'guarded act satisfied' (G2): not defined; unstated satisfaction handled only by F1 (reserve), absent in Gate 1
per-act code of an unguarded act (G2 'none UNTESTABLE'): not defined
'act' (G1, G2): defined in F2 (reserve only); Gate 1 has only §A's loose description
'refusal' / 'cites a rule' (G1, G3, D-V1): not defined; relation to REJECT and to per-act coding unclear
'the problem' in G4's definition of 'demonstrated need'
'slice' / 'successor slice' (G4 gives a trigger, not a definition)
'authority' / 'act of an authority' / 'actor' (G5): not defined; no code for a named non-authority actor
'looser' (G and F override clauses): no ordering defined
f_dependency: Implicit, not explicit: no G rule cites §F, but G2 relies on F1 (per-act UNTESTABLE when guard satisfaction unstated), G1/G2 rely on F2 (definition of act), G5 relies on F4 (evidence bearing on a decision). In the Gate 1 manual G is applicable but less determinate, and the same record can code differently under the two r3 manuals.
